thread.title: Foreign Exchange / Money Transfer Outlook: Mid-Terms, FOMC and RBA all feature in a Big Week for Markets

author: James Elliot
title: Foreign Exchange / Money Transfer Outlook: Mid-Terms, FOMC and RBA all feature in a Big Week for Markets
text:
Foreign Exchange / Money Transfer Outlook: Mid-Terms, FOMC And RBA All Feature In A Big Week For Markets Foreign Exchange / Money Transfer Outlook: Mid-Terms, FOMC And RBA All Feature In A Big Week For Markets Facebook Political uncertainty will come to an end this week as the mid-term elections in the US are due Tuesday, with results due early Wednesday morning.
FOMC is due on Thursday, and while a rate hike is unlikely, all eyes will be on this meeting as the Fed is currently one of the big concerns for the markets.
The RBA policy statement, UK GDP also feature, and trade talk chatter will be high going into the elections.
Market volatility is sure to stay high this week. Earnings season will quieten down after peaking with Apple (AAPL) earnings last week, but politics will be the big driver as US Mid-term elections are due over Tuesday and Wednesday. The most bullish outcome will probably come from a Republican sweep, but this is very unlikely and the odds for the Republicans losing the House but retaining the Senate are both 85%. The last election in 2016 and the subsequent market reaction tells us anything can happen.
Last week’s NFP data could still dictate early Monday trading and there is light selling to start the week with the Dow Jones down -0.25% in futures trading. Jobs data came in very strong which supports the idea the Fed can only get tighter. The US dollar is largely flat, and the EURUSD is still hanging around the 1.13 level despite holding convincingly during last week’s test of this support. The more it stays in this area and tests this level the more likely it breaks at some stage.
As well as the Mid-terms, central bank meetings from the RBA and the FOMC will also feature, and trade deal chatter still seems to be moving markets in both directions.
Monday November 05
Daylight Saving ends in the US, bringing it back into line with Europe. Today the US reimposes some tariffs on Iran. Eurozone finance ministers meet in Brussels. President Xi is scheduled to speak during the China International Import Expo and traders will be watching for any comment on the trade war. Also on today are BoJ Governor Kuroda, BoC Governor Poloz, and ECB Vice President Guindos. Russian markets are closed for Unity Day.
Tuesday November 06
The RBA statement for last month will be released early morning on Tuesday. But the main event is the US mid-term elections and there will be a nervous wait until results early Wednesday morning. ECB Lautenschlaeger speaks at 12:00. One normally unimportant release, the Spanish Markit Services print < at 08:15 is significant. The estimate is 51.8, the lowest for years, and a move below 50 (the point between expansion and contraction) could have a severe effect on the IBEX and Spanish bonds.
Wednesday November 07
The mid-term polls close at 0100, and enough results should be in by 0500 to determine the composition of Congress. Expect a wild ride on ES and YM futures in the Asian session. It is expected that the US Section 232 report on the auto industry results will be announced, leading to further auto tariffs. ECB trade chief Cecilia Malmstrom speaks today in Brussels. Indian markets start a two day Diwali holiday for the third and final days of the religious festival.
Thursday November 08
The FOMC rate set meeting is unusually on Thursday this month, rather than the usual Wednesday. A hold is expected, although surprisingly, there is a 7.2% chance (higher than usual) of a hike, per the CME FedWatch tool. The only significant (to indices) earnings report this week is DIS, after the bell. India is closed again.
Friday November 09
Events and data are somewhat quieter today, and markets will almost certainly still be reacting to the mid-terms and the Fed. The main releases of the day are UK GDP at 09:30 and the RBA Monertay Policy Statement. Fed Quarles (centrist, 2018 and 2019 voter) speaks at 13:15.
